versions.text: Anything that is forbidden on Shabbat—whether because it is similar to work or it [may] bring one to [do] work or it is because of a Shabbat decree—is certainly forbidden on a holiday, unless there was something about it for the sake of eating and that which is similar to it. And anything that is permissible on Shabbat is permissible on a holiday. But there is the prohibition on a holiday of muktseh (that which is designated) which is not found on Shabbat—as muktseh is forbidden on a holiday, but permissible on Shabbat. Because a holiday is less weighty than Shabbat, [the Sages] forbade muktseh upon it, lest one would come to make light of it.
